note: Generated by TestWriteStatementDomainSignatureMaterial (sdn-server/internal/modulert). Go is authoritative for every signature and preimage here; stage 2 (the SDK writer) only wraps them in a publication trailer.

registry.description: update manifest, canonical manifest SHA-256 (reserved; no producer yet)

artifacts.name: domain-signed-ok
artifacts.why: the node-signed form: signature covers domain||0x00||sha256(portable)

artifacts.name: domain-signed-ok-whitespace-padded-domain
artifacts.why: declared domain is whitespace-padded; both sides TrimSpace before comparing

artifacts.name: domain-signed-ok-nel-padded-domain
artifacts.why: U+0085 NEL pads the domain: Go's strings.TrimSpace strips it and JS's String.trim does NOT, so this vector is the whole reason the SDK trims Go's whitespace set explicitly

artifacts.name: domain-bom-padded-is-refused
artifacts.why: U+FEFF BOM pads the domain: JS's String.trim strips it and Go's does NOT, so a naive JS verifier would ACCEPT what the node refuses

artifacts.name: domain-signed-ok-uppercase-algorithm
artifacts.why: the node compares the algorithm with EqualFold after TrimSpace; an exact-match verifier would refuse what the node admits

artifacts.name: bare-digest-labelled-with-domain
artifacts.why: regression gate on the whole design: a bare-digest signature must not pass as a domain-separated one

artifacts.name: foreign-registered-domain
artifacts.why: cross-domain replay: an update-manifest signature must not be admissible as a module signature

artifacts.name: foreign-registered-domain-untrusted-signer
artifacts.why: ORDER pin: what the signature covers is resolved BEFORE who signed it, so the reason is the domain, not the signer

artifacts.name: unregistered-domain
artifacts.why: the registry is CLOSED: an unknown label is refused even though its preimage is well-formed

artifacts.name: domain-signed-untrusted-signer
artifacts.why: a perfectly formed domain signature from a key nobody trusts is still refused

artifacts.name: domain-signed-tampered-payload
artifacts.why: payload mutated after signing; the declared content hash no longer matches the bytes

artifacts.name: legacy-bare-digest-no-domain
artifacts.why: pre-domain SDK artifacts keep verifying byte-for-byte: zero blast radius on the live admit path

artifacts.name: bundle-scope-signed-ok
artifacts.why: bundle scope: the signature covers the canonical whole-bundle statement, NOT sha256(portable) — sdn-server compared it against sha256(portable) unconditionally and reported hash_mismatch for an artifact the SDK and kubo both verified

artifacts.name: bundle-scope-untrusted-signer
artifacts.why: same bundle artifact, empty trust set: every implementation must refuse for the SIGNER, not for the hash basis

artifacts.name: bundle-scope-recorded-digest-tampered
artifacts.why: the recorded signedHashHex no longer matches the recomputed bundle statement digest: hash_mismatch, and it must be reported against the BUNDLE digest rather than against sha256(portable)

artifacts.name: domain-and-bundle-algorithm-is-ambiguous
artifacts.why: declares a statement domain AND the bundle hash algorithm: two different preimages, so the artifact has not said what its signature covers. Resolving it either way silently discards the other claim — kubo resolved bundle-first, which would have dropped the cross-domain replay guard

artifacts.name: statement-domain-key-case-variant-is-refused
artifacts.why: spells the key StatementDomain: Go's decoder matched it case-insensitively and took the domain path, while JS read payload.statementDomain, saw nothing and fell to the legacy path — the node verified what the SDK refused
